tests.notes: compiles successfully; checkedAdd(200, 100) reverts with Panic(0x11) while uncheckedAdd(200, 100) == 44 (wraps at the operand width, 8 bits)
compiles successfully; checkedSub(0, 1) reverts with Panic(0x11) while uncheckedSub(0, 1) wraps to type(uint256).max
compiles successfully; checkedMul(16, 16) reverts with Panic(0x11) while the unchecked uint256 form returns the low 256 bits of the product
compiles successfully; checkedPow(2, 8) reverts with Panic(0x11) while uncheckedPow(2, 8) == 0 for uint8
compiles successfully; ++ and -- (prefix and postfix) revert at the boundary in checked context and wrap in unchecked context
compiles successfully; unchecked int8 add/sub/mul wrap in two's complement (127 + 1 == -128) while the checked versions revert with Panic(0x11)
compiles successfully; checkedNeg(-128) reverts with Panic(0x11) while uncheckedNeg(-128) == -128
compiles successfully; checkedDiv(-128, -1) reverts with Panic(0x11) while uncheckedDiv(-128, -1) returns type(int8).min
compiles successfully; compound assignment operators obey the surrounding checked or unchecked context
compiles successfully; unchecked applies only to arithmetic written inside the block: a checked callee still reverts and an unchecked callee still wraps from checked code
compiles successfully; arithmetic after the closing brace of an unchecked block is checked again in the same function
compiles successfully; inside unchecked even intermediate results wrap so (a + b) - b recovers a; the checked version reverts at the intermediate overflow
unchecked ++i as the loop increment while the accumulated total stays checked; sum(5) == 10
compiles successfully; / and % by a runtime zero still revert with Panic(0x12) inside unchecked, because that check cannot be disabled
variables can be declared and used inside an unchecked block; results are carried out through an outer variable
a variable declared inside an unchecked block is not visible after the closing brace
unchecked is only valid as a block statement; it cannot prefix a single statement
unchecked affects runtime arithmetic only; 255 + 1 is folded to exactly 256 at compile time and does not fit uint8 regardless of unchecked
